meta.title: Colorado local fee reductions and land-use incentives for affordable housing
meta.method: Curated, not a feed. Each entry was read from the jurisdiction's (or its utility's or district's) own code, resolution, fee schedule, council record or program page, saved, and every evidence quote was checked by exact substring match against the saved text (whitespace normalised). verification.level "primary" means checked against that primary document; "reported" means taken from a named reproduction or outlet without the primary document. Every dollar amount and percentage an entry states appears in its own evidence quotes (tests/test_fee_reductions.py). An amount the source does not publish is null, never 0. Measures are kept separate: waived (not owed), reduced (partly owed), reimbursed (paid, then paid back), deferred (still owed, paid later — not a cost reduction), and rate_discount (a recurring utility bill discount, not a development cost). backfill records how a waived amount is paid for only when the source says so; otherwise not_specified. kind says whether an entry is a standing program, a one-off project_award (an example of what a jurisdiction has done, not an offer), or repealed (kept for the record). A county entry may apply only outside town limits. This is screening context, not a study: it lists what a jurisdiction offers, not what any project will receive.

legal_basis.citation: Colo. Const. art. X, §20(2)(b),(2)(d) (TABOR)
legal_basis.summary: TABOR excludes enterprises from 'district' and defines an enterprise as a government-owned business authorized to issue its own revenue bonds and receiving under 10% of annual revenue in grants from all Colorado state and local governments combined; Legislative Council Staff explains that enterprise revenue is not counted toward the TABOR limit and gives an example (State Fair Authority) of an entity that lost enterprise status by receiving more than 10 percent of revenue from state and local governments. Implication (from the text): a utility enterprise that is paid large general-fund grants to cover waived tap/PIF revenue risks crossing the 10% grant threshold and losing its TABOR exclusion.

evidence.quote: "District" means the state or any local government, excluding enterprises.
"Enterprise" means a government-owned business authorized to issue its own revenue bonds and receiving under 10% of annual revenue in grants from all Colorado state and local governments combined.

An enterprise may receive up to 10 percent of its annual revenue from state and local government sources combined. Otherwise, an enterprise must be financially independent of the state or any local government. In addition, an enterprise must have authority to issue its own revenue bonds.
When a program is granted enterprise status, its revenue is not counted toward the TABOR limit calculation.

legal_basis.summary: A water activity enterprise is a government water business owned by a district that receives under ten percent of its annual revenues in grants from all Colorado state and local governments combined and can issue its own revenue bonds; such enterprises are excluded from TABOR. 'Grant' is defined as a non-repayable cash payment of public funds, but excludes public funds paid in exchange for an agreement by the enterprise to provide services including the provision of water or capacity of project works.
